quiz.q: Which item is NOT part of a complete pricing sheet?
quiz.explain: A pricing sheet covers cost, market, value, chosen price, offers and dates. Competitors' personal details are not needed.

quiz.q: A seller's cost-plus price is above the whole market range. What is a sensible first step?
options: Check for cost savings, a smaller size or clear extra value
Sell below cost to gain customers
quiz.explain: If cost-plus is above the market, she must lower costs, change the offer or show extra value.

quiz.q: True cost rises from ₦1,000 to ₦1,200. She wants to keep a 25% margin. What new price does the formula give?
What is the most respectful way to introduce a price increase to regular customers?
options: Change the price without telling anyone
Give notice, explain briefly and honour orders already placed
Raise the price only for customers who look wealthy
quiz.explain: Early notice, a short honest reason and honouring agreed orders keep trust.

quiz.q: Her monthly margin has fallen from 31% to 24% while sales stayed the same. What has most likely happened?
options: Her costs have risen or she is giving more discounts
quiz.explain: Steady sales with a falling margin usually means rising costs or extra discounts. Time to recalculate.

quiz.q: Which is the best evidence for the selling-conversation part of the capstone?
options: A general statement that she is good at selling
A script or note of a real or practised conversation and what she learned
A photo of her shop sign
quiz.explain: The capstone asks for documentation of a real or practised conversation, with honest reflection.

finalQuiz.q: Which list gives the three groups that make up true cost?
finalQuiz.explain: True cost = direct costs (materials, packaging) + labour (your time) + a share of overhead (rent, data, transport).

finalQuiz.q: A batch costs ₦24,000 and gives 50 items, of which 2 are usually spoiled. What is the true cost per good item?
A buyer sends an SMS alert for ₦25,000, but your banking app balance has not changed. What do you do?
options: Release the goods; the SMS is enough
Ask for your OTP to verify
Keep the goods until the money shows in your balance, and offer POS or cash
finalQuiz.explain: SMS alerts and screenshots can be faked. Only money visible in your balance in your own app is proof.

finalQuiz.q: Cost ₦800, price ₦1,200. What is the margin?
Kemi wants a 40% margin on an item that truly costs ₦1,500. Which price is correct?
Seller X sells 300 g of groundnuts for ₦900. Seller Y sells 500 g for ₦1,400. Which is cheaper per 100 g?
Price ₦2,000, true cost ₦1,500. After a 10% discount, how many times more items must she sell to keep the same total profit?
finalQuiz.explain: Profit falls from ₦500 to ₦300 (₦1,800 − ₦1,500). ₦500 ÷ ₦300 = 1.67, so she needs about two-thirds more sales just to stand still.

finalQuiz.q: Which offer usually protects profit best on 10 items priced ₦800 with a true cost of ₦550?
In a selling conversation, what should you do right after stating your price?
options: Stop talking and let the customer respond
finalQuiz.explain: State the price with a benefit, then pause. Apologising or discounting straight away weakens a fair price.

finalQuiz.q: A customer says your gown price is too expensive. Using the four-step method, what comes after listening and acknowledging?
options: Ask a clarifying question about the real concern
Tell her she cannot afford it
finalQuiz.explain: Listen, acknowledge, ask, then respond. Asking reveals whether the issue is budget, comparison or doubt about value.

finalQuiz.q: Market levy and kiosk rent total ₦36,000 a month. Profit per item is ₦240. What is the break-even quantity per month?
finalQuiz.explain: Break-even = fixed costs ÷ profit per item = ₦36,000 ÷ ₦240 = 150 items.

finalQuiz.q: In her monthly review, Zainab's sales are steady but margin has dropped from 30% to 22%. What should her 90-day plan say to do first?
options: Recalculate true cost and check discounts, then adjust price or offer
Lower the price to sell more
finalQuiz.explain: Steady sales with a falling margin signals rising costs or more discounting. Recalculate, then decide and communicate any change.

capstone.title: Pricing & Selling Confidence Project
capstone.brief: Price one real product or service properly and show that you can sell it. You will produce a one-page pricing sheet with a calculated true cost and a considered price with genuine margin, documentation of a real or practised selling conversation using that price, and a 90-day plan for reviewing and refining your price as costs and the market change.
steps: Choose one product or service you sell or will sell, and write its current or planned price.
Calculate its true cost per item from real receipts, timed labour, overhead and waste (Module 1).
Survey at least five competitors, compare prices per unit, and list the value points customers mention (Module 2).
Choose your price, show its profit, markup and margin, and set bulk, promotion and walk-away prices that stay above cost (Module 4, Lesson 1).
Hold a real or practised selling conversation using your five-stage script; note what was said, any objections and how you responded (Module 3).
Write a 90-day review plan with dated actions, the input prices you will watch and the triggers for changing your price (Module 4, Lesson 3).
evidence: Completed one-page pricing sheet with cost groups, market range, value points, chosen price, margin and walk-away price
Before-and-after comparison of your old and new price with a one-sentence reason
Selling script plus a note or voice note of a real or practised conversation, with honest reflection
At least one week of daily sales records at the new price (if you have started selling)
Written 90-day plan with review dates set in your phone calendar
